findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the Approach, address ADR-0043's explicit rejection of structured evidence metadata — state the positive rationale for a DET-parsed provenance grammar over stating the three facts in the attestation prose (which the AGENT criterion already reads), so the alternative is visibly weighed rather than silently overridden.
evidence: ADR-0043 §Alternatives: 'A machine-readable criterion-kind field (structured per-criterion metadata) instead of an inline prompt tag. Rejected: the admissible evidence is unavoidably natural language … that only the LLM can judge for substance, so a structured flag removes no judgment'
Approach §1a pins a `key=value; key=value` grammar with a DET parser/placeholder-rejector — precisely the structured-metadata shape the parent ADR declined for attestation evidence

The AGENT criterion already reads the checkbox item to judge the environment-vs-IaC contradiction, so it could also judge presence of the three facts stated in prose — making the DET grammar's marginal value narrower than the plan implies
findings.finding: The Approach adds a DET-parsed STRUCTURED continuation-line grammar for provenance, but ADR-0043 — the ADR this story amends — explicitly considered and REJECTED a machine-readable structured metadata field for this same evidence surface in favour of natural-language attestation the LLM judges for substance. The plan does not engage that rejection or justify why structured fields are the right shape here, leaving a plausibly-superior alternative (provenance stated in the attestation prose, judged by the AGENT criterion that already reads it) unweighed.
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer asks why this story reintroduces the structured-metadata shape ADR-0043 rejected, and the plan has no recorded answer
Author friction: a rigid single-line grammar with em-dash + exact keys is more brittle to author than free-text provenance the LLM parses

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ground the measurement-provenance schema in prior art: have the new ADR cite ADR-0046 and ADR-0049 (and the SLSA/in-toto environment/principal/isolation provenance model they already reference), and note explicitly how the three fields relate to — or deliberately depart from — that established predicate shape, rather than citing only ADR-0043.
evidence: Plan invents fields: 'environment — the concrete identifier ...; principal — the identity the measurement ran as; privilege_posture — one of production-equivalent / broader / narrower' — the same environment/identity/isolation axes SLSA/in-toto provenance predicates model.

Web search (retrieved): SLSA/in-toto provenance attestation records 'data about the build environment', and an in-toto layout defines 'Which identities are authorized to perform each step' plus SLSA Build L3 'build environment isolation' — the environment/principal/privilege triad the plan reinvents.

Repo ADR-0046 line 55: the plan's G6 boundary is verbatim in-repo prior art — 'This is the same scoping every provenance system draws (SLSA states it explicitly: provenance proves how an artifact was produced, not that its inputs were good)' — yet the plan re-derives it without citation.

Repo ADR-0049 lines 203-208 and ADR-0046 lines 192-193 carry explicit 'Prior art / grounding' sections citing 'in-toto / SLSA ... non-falsifiable provenance produced by a trusted control plane' — the plan's ADR cites only ADR-0043.
ABSENCE: the plan has no prior-art/grounding discussion for the provenance-field schema despite crossing a security/provenance bright-line.
findings.finding: The plan invents a three-field measurement-provenance schema (environment / principal / privilege_posture) and mandates a new ADR, but considers no prior art for it — neither the established SLSA/in-toto provenance-attestation model (whose environment / authorized-identity / build-isolation axes the three fields mirror) nor the repo's OWN provenance ADRs (0046, 0049) which already carry 'Prior art / grounding' sections citing in-toto/SLSA and already state the exact honest-provenance boundary the plan re-derives from scratch in its G6 rejection. The new ADR is scoped to cite ADR-0043 only.
findings.location: ## Scope ('docs/adr/ — an ADR recording the amended evidence contract, citing ADR-0043 as the shape it changes') and ## Explicitly rejected (G6 honest-declaration limit)
scenarios: The new ADR ships citing only ADR-0043, diverging from the repo's own ADR convention (0046/0049) of grounding provenance decisions against in-toto/SLSA, and re-deriving the honest-provenance boundary as if novel.
A reviewer or future author cannot tell whether the three-field schema deliberately departs from, or is unaware of, the established SLSA/in-toto predicate model.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Scope 'docs/adr/' line and the G6 rejection, add that the new ADR situates environment/principal/privilege_posture against the established SLSA/in-toto provenance predicate axes and against rebar's own provenance ADRs (0046's 'provenance proves how, not that inputs were good' boundary, which is exactly the G6 limit; 0049's non-falsifiable-provenance grounding), citing them alongside ADR-0043.

findings.finding: The plan does not specify the textual form or location of the three provenance fields (environment / principal / privilege_posture + one-line justification) within the ticket, yet both the deterministic presence check and the AGENT contradiction probe depend on locating them — and, for the DET check, associating them with their owning [operator-attested] AC item.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that the three fields are authored as an indented sub-block immediately following the `[operator-attested]` checkbox line (the AC item they belong to), give the exact key spelling, and have det_measurement_provenance parse that sub-block per AC item — extending det_operator_attested's ac_item_lines to also capture each item's continuation/sub-bullet lines rather than only the checkbox line.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a deterministic `trigger` to `project.measurement-provenance` in `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` (e.g. text_all matching `operator-attested` + `provenance:`) so the AGENT-tier contradiction probe only routes on plans that actually carry a provenance declaration, and update the structural AC to assert the trigger is present.
evidence: orchestrator.py:298-309 routes a project criterion whose `project_trigger_fires` returns None (absent trigger) unconditionally into the `agent` list — fail-open, no gate
det_gate_rules.py:174-183: `project_trigger_fires` returns None (fail-open, 'must not gate') when `trigger` is absent
registry.AGENT_TIER doc: 'one tool-using agent loop each; ~85× a single-turn call'

The sibling `project.engine-layer-enforcement` overlay entry (.rebar/criteria_routing.json) DOES carry a deterministic `trigger`; this new criterion's activation condition (an `[operator-attested]` item + a `provenance:` line) is deterministically detectable — the plan already builds that scanner for its DET check
The plan's own no-anchor / grandfathering cases mean the criterion's only output on a plan with no provenance declaration is NO finding — pure cost
findings.finding: The new AGENT-tier criterion `project.measurement-provenance` has no deterministic `trigger`, so it will route on every plan reaching Pass-1 rather than only on plans carrying an `[operator-attested]` provenance declaration — paying an ~85×-single-turn-cost tool-using agent loop to produce a no-finding on the majority of plans that have no provenance line at all.
findings.location: Scope › `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` bullet; and the AC `python3 -c "...assert d['plan_review'][c]['exec']=='AGENT'"` (which omits any trigger)
scenarios: Every ordinary plan-review run in a repo with the overlay active pays one extra AGENT loop that can only return not-applicable
Cost/latency regression across the whole gate, not just tickets exercising the new rule
findings.suggested_fix: Give the routing entry a `trigger` conjunction keyed on `[operator-attested]` AND `provenance:` vocabulary (parity with `project.engine-layer-enforcement`'s trigger), and extend the structural AC's `python3 -c` assertion to require `d['plan_review'][c].get('trigger')`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the leaf's provenance contract with the parent epic's recorded requirement to capture instrument-KIND (simulation / static analysis / live call): either add a fourth declared field to E1's contract and its DET/AGENT checks, or update parent 3147 to descope instrument-kind (which restages the parent's plan-review) so leaf and parent agree.
evidence: Parent epic 3147 comment (design decision on the parent's current/final state): 'the measurement-provenance contract should capture not only WHERE and UNDER WHAT PRIVILEGE a measurement was taken, but what KIND of instrument produced it (simulation / static analysis / live call) — because a simulation and a live call are not interchangeable evidence for an authorization claim, and the current attestation shape cannot tell them apart.'

Leaf defines exactly three fields and no fourth: 'provenance: environment=<value>; principal=<value>; privilege_posture=<production-equivalent|broader|narrower> — <one-line justification>' — instrument-kind is absent from the pinned canonical form, from Approach step 1, and from every AC.
Sibling session log 233f: 'Preflight PASS for all three epics: 3147 (1 child: f161)' — the epic has a single child, so the instrument-kind capture cannot be assigned to a sibling story.

This is the parent's self-described sharpest escape (2b): S9249 records that a role-scoped simulate-principal-policy produced a confident WRONG authorization conclusion that only a real from-instance call refuted — privilege_posture cannot distinguish a simulation from a live call at the same posture, so the three fields do not cover this class.

Tension noted: the parent's approach point 1 and its four ACs list only environment/principal/privilege posture; the instrument-kind requirement appears in the parent's comment, not its ACs — so this is an omission of a parent-recorded deliverable rather than a contradiction of a parent AC.
findings.finding: The leaf's provenance contract omits an instrument-kind field (simulation / static analysis / live call) that the parent epic's own recorded design decision says the measurement-provenance contract MUST capture; because the epic has exactly one child (this leaf), no sibling can deliver it.
findings.location: E1 Approach step 1 / '1a. The declaration's exact textual form' / Scope — the three-field contract (environment; principal; privilege_posture)
scenarios: An author attests a scoped-IAM criterion 'verified by aws iam simulate-principal-policy' at privilege_posture: production-equivalent; the leaf's contract records posture but cannot record that the instrument was a simulator, so the exact S9249 escape (simulator answered a different question than the service checks) passes the amended contract undeclared.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a fourth key to the pinned declaration form (e.g. `instrument=<simulation|static-analysis|live-call>`) with matching placeholder/shape rules in det_measurement_provenance.py and a rubric decision rule, OR edit the parent epic to record that instrument-kind is deferred/out-of-scope and remove it from the contract intent so the leaf remains a true subset.
